intro.title: List Virtualization
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Vue component that efficiently displays a large list of items using list virtualization. You will learn how to render only the visible items on the screen, which improves performance by reducing the number of DOM elements. The core concept involves calculating which items are in the viewport and dynamically updating the list as the user scrolls. You will use Vue's reactive state, computed properties, and event handlers to implement this technique in a single-file component.
intro.usecase: List virtualization is essential for handling large datasets in modern web applications. You'll see this pattern in social media feeds that display thousands of posts, e-commerce product catalogs with extensive filtering, and data dashboards showing real-time analytics. As a Vue developer, implementing virtualization ensures smooth scrolling and responsive interactions when building admin panels, financial transaction lists, or any interface where performance matters with massive datasets.
